what_this_is: The hand adjudication of all 46 recital atoms extracted by measure.py. No line of this file is computed; every row is a judgement made by reading the recital and then reading the 99 articles, and every row that claims an article counterpart quotes it. Rows that claim there is none say so in those words. This file is the night's judgement layer and it is the part a reader should disagree with first.

classes.safeguard: a concrete thing a data subject, or a body they have mandated, may demand under this Regulation
classes.general: a restatement of the fundamental right to the protection of personal data, not a specific safeguard
classes.external: a right conferred by another instrument -- the Charter, the TFEU -- referred to here rather than granted here
classes.third-party-duty: a norm addressed to somebody who is not the data subject and not, in the operative text, a duty-bearer
classes.artefact: the extractor ran past the right into an adjacent clause; the string is not a right at all

verdicts.matched: an article grants the same thing in substantially the same words
verdicts.reworded: an article grants the same thing in different words -- the case a string match gets wrong
verdicts.unmatched: no article of the Regulation contains it
verdicts.n/a: the class makes the question meaningless

rows.atom: the protection of personal data concerning him or her
rows.note: recital 1 restates Article 8(1) of the Charter; Article 1(2) GDPR: 'This Regulation protects fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons and in particular their right to the protection of personal data.'

rows.atom: the protection of personal data
rows.note: same restatement

rows.atom: the protection of personal data is not an absolute right; it must be considered in relation to its function in society ...
rows.note: a proposition about the standing of the right, drawn from the Court's case law. No article says it. It is not a safeguard, so it is not counted as an unmatched one -- but it is a statement of law that lives only in the half with no binding force.

rows.atom: an effective remedy
rows.note: item in recital 4's list of Charter rights the Regulation respects; conferred by Article 47 of the Charter

rows.atom: a fair trial, and cultural, religious and linguistic diversity
rows.note: same list; the atom boundary is the extractor's, not the text's

rows.atom: the protection of personal data, with regard to the processing ... may prevent the free flow ...
rows.note: the extractor ran from 'right to the protection of personal data' into the sentence's main clause about legal fragmentation

rows.atom: obtain confirmation and communication of personal data concerning them which are being processed
rows.quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed, and, where that is the case, access to the personal data
rows.note: 'confirmation' survives into the article; 'communication' does not -- the article says 'access' and, at 15(3), 'a copy'

rows.atom: object, should be ensured
rows.quote: The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her

rows.atom: object
rows.quote: Article 21 Right to object

rows.atom: know and obtain communication in particular with regard to the purposes for which the personal data are processed ...
rows.quote: access to the personal data and the following information: (a) the purposes of the processing;
rows.note: the recital's verbs -- 'know', 'obtain communication' -- appear nowhere in Article 15, which says 'obtain ... confirmation', 'access' and 'the following information'. Same right, different words.

rows.atom: have personal data concerning him or her rectified and a 'right to be forgotten' ...
rows.quote: Article 17 Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
rows.note: the quotation marks around the phrase are in both texts

rows.atom: be forgotten' where the retention of such data infringes this Regulation or Union or Member State law ...
rows.quote: the personal data have been unlawfully processed
rows.note: 'infringes this Regulation' in the recital, 'unlawfully processed' in the article

rows.atom: have his or her personal data erased and no longer processed where the personal data are no longer necessary ...
rows.quote: the personal data are no longer necessary in relation to the purposes for which they were collected or otherwise processed

rows.atom: be forgotten in the online environment, the right to erasure should also be extended ...
rows.quote: the controller ... shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal data that the data subject has requested the erasure

rows.atom: erasure should also be extended in such a way that a controller who has made the personal data public should be obliged to inform ...
rows.quote: Where the controller has made the personal data public and is obliged pursuant to paragraph 1 to erase the personal data, the controller ... shall take reasonable steps ... to inform controllers

rows.atom: transmit or receive personal data concerning him or her should not create an obligation for the controllers to adopt or maintain processing systems which are technically compatible
rows.note: A LIMIT ON THE RIGHT, STATED ONLY IN THE PREAMBLE. Article 20 contains the words 'where technically feasible' (20(2)) and 'shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others' (20(4)), and nothing about an obligation to adopt or maintain technically compatible systems. 'technically compatible' occurs once in the 173 recitals and zero times in the 99 articles. Classed as a third-party duty rather than a safeguard because its beneficiary is the controller, not the data subject -- it is a norm relieving somebody of a duty, published where it has no binding force.

rows.atom: receive the personal data should be without prejudice to the rights and freedoms of other data subjects
rows.quote: The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
rows.note: 'without prejudice to' in the recital, 'shall not adversely affect' in the article

rows.atom: have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another
rows.quote: the data subject shall have the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible
rows.note: word for word, except that the article adds the condition

rows.atom: object to such processing, including profiling to the extent that it is related to such direct marketing ...
rows.quote: the data subject shall have the right to object at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her for such marketing, which includes profiling to the extent that it is related to such direct marketing

rows.atom: not to be subject to a decision, which may include a measure, evaluating personal aspects ...
rows.quote: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning him or her or similarly significantly affects him or her
rows.note: the recital's 'which may include a measure' is not in the article

rows.atom: obtain human intervention
rows.quote: the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller

rows.atom: express his or her point of view
rows.quote: to express his or her point of view

rows.atom: obtain an explanation of the decision reached after such assessment
rows.note: THE CASE. Article 22(3) carries three of recital 71's four safeguards and not this one. The word 'explanation' occurs once in the 173 recitals and zero times in the 99 articles; 'explain' occurs zero times in both. Article 15(1)(h) instead grants 'meaningful information about the logic involved'. In C-203/22, CK v Dun & Bradstreet Austria, 27 February 2025, the Court of Justice read recital 71's purpose into Article 15(1)(h) and held that the provision 'affords the data subject a genuine right to an explanation' -- the content of a norm published without binding force becoming enforceable through a neighbour, without being republished.

rows.atom: challenge the decision
rows.quote: and to contest the decision
rows.note: THE FALSE POSITIVE. 'challenge' occurs 5 times in the recitals and 0 times in the articles; 'contest' occurs 0 times in the recitals and 2 times in the articles. This is the only atom of the 46 that the mechanical rule flags, and it is the one atom that is wrong -- the right is granted, in another verb.

rows.atom: data portability, the right to object, decisions based on profiling, as well as the communication of a personal data breach ...
rows.note: recital 73 lists the rights that Union or Member State law may RESTRICT; the extractor took the list as a grant. Article 23 is the operative counterpart.

rows.atom: object, decisions based on profiling, as well as the communication of a personal data breach ...
rows.note: the same sentence, split again at the next coordinated 'right to'

rows.atom: data protection when developing and designing such products, services and applications ... with due regard to the state of the art
rows.note: A DUTY ON AN ACTOR THE OPERATIVE TEXT NEVER BINDS. The recital's sentence reads 'producers of the products, services and applications should be encouraged to take into account the right to data protection when developing and designing such products'. Article 25, Data protection by design and by default, addresses 'the controller' and nobody else; the word 'producers' occurs once in the 173 recitals and zero times in the 99 articles. The recital also uses 'should be encouraged' -- an exhortation, which Guideline 10 forbids in recitals by name.

rows.atom: make sure that controllers and processors are able to fulfil their data protection obligations
rows.note: the purpose clause of the producers sentence, split off as if it were a coordinated right

rows.atom: lodge a complaint with a single supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of his or her habitual residence ...
rows.quote: every data subject shall have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of his or her habitual residence
rows.note: the recital's 'single' is not in the article

rows.atom: an effective judicial remedy in accordance with Article 47 of the Charter if the data subject considers that his or her rights ... are infringed
rows.quote: each data subject shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy where he or she considers that his or her rights under this Regulation have been infringed

rows.atom: mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association which is constituted in accordance with the law of a Member State ...
rows.quote: The data subject shall have the right to mandate a not-for-profit body, organisation or association which has been properly constituted in accordance with the law of a Member State

rows.atom: a judicial remedy on behalf of data subjects or, if provided for in Member State law, exercise the right to receive compensation ...
rows.quote: to exercise the rights referred to in Articles 77, 78 and 79 on his or her behalf, and to exercise the right to receive compensation referred to in Article 82 on his or her behalf where provided for by Member State law

rows.atom: receive compensation on behalf of data subjects
rows.quote: the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered

rows.atom: lodge a complaint in that Member State, independently of a data subject's mandate ...
rows.quote: any body, organisation or association referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, independently of a data subject's mandate, has the right to lodge, in that Member State, a complaint with the supervisory authority

rows.atom: an effective judicial remedy where it has reasons to consider that the rights of a data subject have been infringed ...
rows.quote: and to exercise the rights referred to in Articles 78 and 79 if it considers that the rights of a data subject under this Regulation have been infringed

rows.atom: bring an action for annulment of decisions of the Board before the Court of Justice under the conditions provided for in Article 263 TFEU
rows.note: conferred by Article 263 TFEU, not by this Regulation; 'annulment' occurs zero times in the 99 articles

rows.atom: an effective judicial remedy does not encompass measures taken by supervisory authorities which are not legally binding ...
rows.quote: each natural or legal person shall have the right to an effective judicial remedy against a legally binding decision of a supervisory authority concerning them
rows.note: the recital states the boundary negatively, the article positively; same boundary

rows.atom: the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation
the protection of personal data with the right to freedom of expression and information, as enshrined in Article 11 of the Charter
rows.quote: Member States shall by law reconcile the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information
rows.note: a duty on Member States rather than a data-subject safeguard, but the article carries it word for word except for the Charter reference

rows.atom: freedom of expression and information, as enshrined in Article 11 of the Charter
rows.note: conferred by Article 11 of the Charter

rows.atom: freedom of expression in every democratic society, it is necessary to interpret notions relating to that freedom, such as journalism, broadly
rows.note: the extractor ran into an interpretive instruction. Worth a second look by a later night: 'it is necessary to interpret ... broadly' is an instruction to a court, published where it has no binding force, and no article says it.

rows.atom: the protection of personal data and may therefore provide for the necessary reconciliation with the right to the protection of personal data ...
the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation
rows.quote: Personal data in official documents ... may be disclosed by the authority or body in accordance with Union or Member State law ... in order to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation

rows.atom: the protection of personal data with an obligation of professional secrecy
rows.quote: to reconcile the right of the protection of personal data with the obligation of secrecy
rows.note: the recital says 'professional secrecy', the article says 'secrecy' at the point of reconciliation

rows.atom: the protection of personal data
ensure the free movement of personal data within the Union, the power to adopt acts in accordance with Article 290 TFEU should be delegated to the Commission
rows.note: the extractor ran from 'their right to the protection of personal data' into the delegation sentence; Article 92 is the operative counterpart of that sentence

totals.totals_note: These numbers were first written by hand from the rows and three of them were wrong -- general 6 for 7, artefact 7 for 6, matched 20 for 19, reworded 6 for 7. adjudicate.py recomputes the totals from the rows and refused to agree with them; the block above is the recomputation and the wrong figures are named here rather than deleted. The rows themselves were not altered.

what_this_census_cannot_see: The atom rule only finds norms phrased as a 'right (not) to'. Three preamble-only norms found by hand while adjudicating are outside its reach and are not in the totals above: recital 27's two sentences excluding deceased persons from the Regulation's scope, which no article contains; recital 71's 'Such measure should not concern a child', which Article 22 does not contain and which is the second preamble-only norm in the very recital this night is about; and recital 68's 'interoperable', a word in the recital's format list that Article 20's format list drops ('interoperab*' occurs twice in the recitals and zero times in the articles). The census is a census of one grammatical form, not of the preamble.
